blocks.source: Vol IV, Deployment Release, § The Verdict's Standing Conditions
blocks.md: A signed release can lapse without any change to the underlying software. Brake linings wear down, camera brackets shift under continuous vibration, or warehouse traffic polishes concrete lanes until traction drops. When these physical premises drift, the stopping claim certified by the adjudicator no longer holds. Standing conditions bind the operational verdict to these physical baselines by defining an explicit observation cadence for each premise alongside deterministic fallback responses when a check fails.

questions.q: The section **The Verdict's Standing Conditions** develops one of the chapter's claims. Which one?
options: An update reopens the claims whose evidence it touches, an unchanged enforcer binary does not imply an unchanged containment argument, and shadow mode filters candidates while contained canaries qualify them.

The release manifest binds every upstream record, the argument digest, binary hashes, calibration, standing conditions, wear budget, expiry, and the adjudicator's signature to one configuration and gates motion fail-closed.

The argument resolves into a signed verdict loaded as the machine's operating permit (UNCOND for the assessed envelope, COND for a separately evidenced restricted limit set, REFUSE naming the next measurement).

When every child claim is required the case is conjunctive and its confidence falls below every premise, so an assessor looks for the least-supported premise, and only genuinely independent sufficient legs add confidence.
